name: SQL Injection
description: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted user input is incorporated into an SQL query without proper validation or parameterization, allowing an attacker to alter the intended SQL statement.
common_causes: Concatenating user input directly into SQL queries
Using string formatting to construct SQL statements
Using f-strings with untrusted input in SQL queries
Using unsafe database APIs that execute dynamically constructed SQL
vulnerable_patterns: SQL query created using string concatenation with user-controlled input
SQL query created using Python format strings with user-controlled input
SQL query created using f-strings with user-controlled input
Raw SQL execution using unsanitized external input

vulnerable_examples.code: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='" + username + "'"
vulnerable_examples.explanation: The username is directly concatenated into the SQL query.

vulnerable_examples.code: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id={user_id}"
vulnerable_examples.explanation: User-controlled input is inserted directly into an SQL statement using an f-string.

secure_patterns: Use database APIs that separate SQL code from user data

secure_examples.explanation: The parameterized query keeps user data separate from the SQL statement.

detection_indicators: User input flows into an SQL query
String concatenation used to construct SQL
Raw SQL execution with external input
Database query contains unsanitized request parameters
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements instead of dynamically concatenating user-controlled input into SQL statements. Use safe database APIs and validate input where appropriate.
